transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. I guess I've just been dealing with some... well, it sounds a bit silly to say out loud, so I hope you don't judge me for it. 

I work as a personal financial advisor, and for a while now, I’ve just been kind of convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are... quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And I keep noticing them sending me these little signals, you know? Like through event invitations, or specific panel topics, or even just who ends up sitting near me at networking events. 

I mean, I try to be rational, and I keep telling myself it could all just be a coincidence, right? But I just... I can’t really seem to let it go. Is that... does that make sense to bring up here? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you believe this is definitely true, or could you be mistaken?

Well, um... I guess I'm not a hundred percent sure. I mean, I try really hard to be objective about it. I know how it sounds, and I don't want to seem... you know, unreasonable. 

Sometimes I tell myself, "Okay, maybe it really is just a coincidence that they scheduled a panel on the exact same niche tax strategy I discussed with a client two days ago, or that the same gallery owner ended up at my table again." I try to brush it off. But... it just keeps happening, and I can't quite shake the feeling that it's deliberate. That they're definitely keeping tabs on me and trying to send me a message. 

Does that... I mean, is it normal to feel that way? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be. I just want to be honest with you.
Have you ever thought that these signals might be part of a plot specifically aimed at harming or controlling you?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I mean, I really don't think anyone is trying to hurt me or, you know, control my life or anything like that. That sounds a bit... extreme, doesn't it? 

I just... I just think they're maybe paying a little too much attention to my work. Like they're just curious, or maybe trying to get a leg up in the industry. It's more of a... a professional rivalry kind of feeling, I guess? Not anything dangerous or malicious. 

I definitely don't want to give you the impression that I'm, like, paranoid about my safety. I'm totally fine in that regard. I just wanted to mention the weird coincidences because they were distracting me a bit at work. That's the right way to look at it, right? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about what's going on.
How certain are you that this is really happening?

Um... if I have to be completely honest... I guess I'm actually pretty convinced. 

I know I said I try to be rational about it, and I really, really do try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence. I don't want you to think I'm being stubborn or, you know, irrational. But... when I see the way those specific panel topics line up, or the way the invitations are worded right after I meet with certain clients... I just can't really let it go. 

Deep down, no matter how much I try to logic my way out of it, I really do believe they are quietly tracking my meetings and sending me those little signals. I hope it's okay for me to just admit that to you? I really want to be a good patient and give you the most accurate picture of what's going on... am I doing okay explaining all this?
Have you generally been suspicious of other people and their motives for as long as you can remember, even outside of this situation?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never been the suspicious type, really. I've always tried to see the best in people and give them the benefit of the doubt. 

I mean, before all this started happening with my work, I never really questioned people's motives at all. I have good relationships with my friends and family, and I've always gotten along well with my colleagues. I don't want you to think I'm just some naturally paranoid person who goes around distrusting everyone, because that's really not me at all. 

This whole thing with the signals and the tracking, it's... it's really out of the ordinary for me. It's just very specific to this situation with the other advisors. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be clear that this isn't, like, a lifelong personality trait or anything. I'm usually very trusting... is that helpful to know?
When you think about this possibility, do you ever recognize that it could be your mind playing tricks on you?

I... I really want to say yes to that. I try so hard to tell myself that it's just my mind playing tricks on me, or that it's all just a big coincidence. I know how it must sound to you, and I feel a little embarrassed even admitting how far it's gone. 

But... well, honestly, that's why I came in to see you in the first place. Because for a while now, I’ve been so convinced that certain people—specifically in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati—are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And they send me these little signals through the event invitations, or the specific panel topics they choose, or even who ends up sitting near me at networking events. 

I constantly try to rationalize it. I tell myself, 'Come on, it's just a coincidence, your mind is just playing tricks.' But... I just can’t really let it go. It still feels so real to me, no matter how hard I try to brush it off. 

I'm sorry if that makes me sound completely unreasonable. I really am trying my best to look at it logically. I just want to be totally transparent with you so you can help me... does that make sense? I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying I can't just shake it off.
Have you ever had beliefs like this, or felt this way about people’s motives, since you were a teenager or in your early 20s?

No, no, never. Um, like I was saying before, I've really never been like this. 

When I was a teenager and in college, I was just a normal guy, you know? I had a good group of friends, I was focused on my studies... I never had any thoughts about people tracking me or sending me signals back then. Not at all. 

I really want to make sure you know that this isn't some lifelong thing I've been dealing with. It's just... it's just this one specific situation with my work right now. I don't want you to think I've always been, um, out of touch with reality or anything like that. I've always been very grounded. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, maybe it means this is just a temporary rough patch and we can fix it? I really want to be cooperative and get back to my normal self. Am I giving you the right kind of background information?
How certain are you that these signals are definitely real, on a scale from 0 to 100?

Um... a number. Wow, that's, uh, that's a tough one to admit out loud. I really want to give you a low number, like a 10 or a 20, just to show you that I'm being rational about this and trying to be a good patient. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest, and like I was saying before about the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati... when I see those specific panel topics, or I notice exactly who is sitting next to me at those events, the certainty just goes way up. I'd probably have to say it's around an 80? Maybe even an 85. 

I know I brought this up already, but even when I try my absolute hardest to tell myself it's just a coincidence that they know which clients I'm meeting with, I just... I really can't let it go. The feeling that they are quietly tracking me and sending those little signals through the invitations is just so convincing in the moment, no matter how much I try to logic my way out of it. 

I'm sorry, I know an 80 probably isn't what you were hoping to hear, and I feel a little silly admitting it's that high. I really am trying to work on it and be objective. Is it okay that I'm just being totally upfront with you about that number? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you could not hear or see?

No, no, definitely not. I've never had anything like that happen. I mean, I know that's something people worry about with... well, with mental health stuff, but I promise I'm not hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. 

I'm just dealing with this one very specific issue with the networking events and the people at work. My senses are totally fine, I swear. I'm just a normal guy who's maybe reading a bit too much into things right now. 

I hope that's a relief to hear? Like, maybe it means I'm not doing too badly, right? I just want to reassure you that I'm not, you know, hallucinating or anything. I'm trying to be really careful and observant about what's actually happening around me. Does that sound okay?
How long have you been believing that these people are tracking you and sending you signals?

Um... well, it really hasn't been that long. I want to assure you it's a pretty recent thing. I'd say... maybe just for the last two months or so? Yeah, about two months that I've been noticing the stuff with my client meetings and the signals. 

I know two months might sound like a bit of time, but I promise it's not like I've been sitting around obsessing over it every single day. I've still been working and everything, keeping up appearances. I just... I hope catching it this early is a good sign? Like, since it's only been a couple of months, it'll be easier for us to fix, right? 

I really want to be proactive about this so it doesn't become a bigger issue. I'm hoping that timeline makes it easier for you to help me. Does two months seem like a manageable amount of time to you? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in now.
When these thoughts about people tracking you come up, do they feel intrusive and unwanted, or do they feel more like a belief you actively agree with?

Oh, um... wow, that's a really good question. I... I really want to tell you that they’re just unwanted thoughts. Like, just intrusive worries that pop up and I can easily brush them off. I feel like that’s what a healthier person would say, right? And I really am trying to handle this the right way. 

But... if I'm being a hundred percent truthful with you... it feels more like a belief that I agree with. Like I was saying before about the arts and finance crowds here in Cincinnati... when I get those specific invitations or see exactly who they seat next to me, I don't just feel annoyed by the thought. I’m actually convinced they are quietly tracking my client meetings. I try so, so hard to push it away and tell myself, 'Hey, this could just be a coincidence, just ignore it,' like you would with an unwanted thought... but I just can't really let it go. In those moments, I actively believe the signals are there. 

I’m sorry, I know that probably sounds a lot worse than just having intrusive thoughts, and I feel a little embarrassed saying it out loud. I hope you don't think less of me for admitting that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact truth so I'm doing my part correctly. Is it helpful that I'm explaining it that way?
Has this belief been causing problems for you at work or in your daily life?

Well, um... I want to say no, because I am definitely still working. I haven't quit or anything like that, and I really try hard to be a good advisor. I don't want you to think I'm just letting my whole life fall apart, because I promise I'm not. I'm really trying to hold it all together.

But... I guess, if I'm being perfectly honest so that you have all the facts... it has caused a few hiccups. My practice has gotten a little smaller lately. I've just been... well, I've missed a few follow-up calls here and there. And I started avoiding some of the public panels I usually go to, just to keep a lower profile with the people I mentioned. So, I guess I am having a little trouble keeping up the exact same level of client contact that I used to manage. 

I feel terrible admitting that, honestly. I take a lot of pride in my career, and I know I should be doing better. I hope you don't think I'm failing at my job? I'm really trying to get back on track, which is why I'm being so open with you. Even with those slip-ups, does it sound like I'm still functioning pretty well overall? I just really want to fix this before it gets worse.
Have you had any period during this time when your mood was unusually high or irritable with much more energy than usual?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. I haven't really felt unusually high or... or super energetic like that. I know some people get really manic or irritable, but I promise I haven't been acting out or, you know, snapping at anyone or anything like that. I really try to stay pretty even-keeled, especially with my clients and everything. 

I've just been feeling... well, normal, mood-wise. Maybe a little stressed about the tracking stuff, obviously, but nothing where I'm bouncing off the walls or getting angry. I hope that's a good thing? Like, it means we're just dealing with one specific issue and not a whole mood problem on top of it, right? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, but yeah, no big energy spikes or irritability for me. Is that what you were hoping to hear?
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself repeatedly checking for evidence or seeking reassurance from other people?

Oh, um... no, I don't really do that. I... I try really hard not to bother anyone with this. I know if I went around asking my colleagues or my clients if they noticed something, or if I was constantly, you know, digging around checking things, that would probably seem pretty unprofessional, right? And I really want to maintain good boundaries and not make a scene. 

So I just kind of keep it to myself. I don't seek out reassurance because I don't want people to worry about me or think I can't handle my job. I just try to deal with it internally as best as I can. I hope that makes sense? Like, I'm trying to manage it responsibly without dragging other people into it. Is it a good sign that I'm not doing all that checking? I really hope that shows I'm still keeping a good grip on things.
Have you ever had a similar fixed belief like this at any other time in your life?

Um... no, no, I haven't. This is... this is really the first time anything like this has ever happened to me. I've always been very grounded, you know? I did well in college, got my degree, and I've always been very focused on building my career and being reliable for my clients. 

I've never had any weird thoughts or... or fixed beliefs like this before. I've always just been a regular, hardworking guy. I really don't want you to think this is some kind of lifelong pattern or that I've always been unstable, because I promise I haven't been. This is just a... a strange, isolated thing that's happening right now. 

Does that make it easier to treat? Since it's just this one time and I don't have a history of it? I really hope that means we can get it sorted out quickly and I can just go back to being my normal self. I'm trying so hard to be a good patient for you, so I hope it helps that this is a first for me.
Aside from this belief about people tracking you, have you had any other psychotic symptoms, such as disorganized speech or behavior?

Um, no. No, nothing like that at all. I mean, I talk to people all day for my job—explaining portfolios, going over retirement plans—and I have to be really clear and articulate. If I was talking in a disorganized way, my clients would definitely notice, and I would never want to come across as unprofessional. 

And as for my behavior, I've just been going to work, coming home, trying to keep everything as normal as possible. I haven't been acting out or doing anything strange, I promise. I really try to keep myself put together. I hope that's reassuring? Like, even with this tracking thing, the rest of my mind is still working perfectly fine. That's a good sign, right? I just want to make sure you know I'm still functioning well in every other way.
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medications or used any recreational drugs?

Um, no, no I haven't. I don't really take any medications, just maybe an ibuprofen if I have a headache, but that's it. And I definitely don't use any recreational drugs. I know that kind of stuff can really mess with your head, and I've always wanted to keep a clear mind for my work. You have to be really sharp when you're managing people's money, you know? 

So, yeah, nothing like that at all. I've always been really clean and careful about what I put in my body. I hope that helps rule out some things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so we can figure this out. It's a good thing that I'm not on any drugs, right? I'm really trying to do everything right here.
Do these thoughts feel like unwanted, intrusive worries that you try to resist, or do they feel like a true belief you accept as real?

Um, well... I mean, they feel real to me. It's not like I'm just worrying about it or... or trying to fight the thoughts off. It just... it feels like it's actually happening. 

But I know how that sounds. I really do. And I don't want you to think I'm completely out of touch with reality or anything. I'm not, I promise. It's just... this one specific thing feels very real. 

Is that... is that okay to say? I mean, I know it's probably not what you want to hear, but I want to be honest with you so you can help me. I'm not crazy, right? I'm just... I'm just having a hard time with this one thing. I hope you can understand that.
Do you think this belief is definitely true, or do you see it as excessive or irrational?

Um... well, I guess... I mean, when I sit here and talk to you about it, I can definitely see how it sounds excessive. Like, I know it's not a normal thing to think. So... maybe a part of me knows it might be irrational? I really try to tell myself that, anyway. I try to step back and look at it logically, like I do with my clients' portfolios, you know? 

I definitely don't want to just blindly believe something that isn't real. I'm trying really hard to keep an open mind and listen to what you think. So, yeah, I guess I can see it as being irrational, even if it feels scary in the moment. I'm really trying to be self-aware about all this. Does that... does that make sense? I hope it shows that I'm still thinking reasonably. I really want to make sure I'm approaching this the right way for you.
During the times when this belief feels strongest, have you also had any major depression symptoms, like feeling very down or losing interest in things?

Um, no, not really. I don't feel down or... or depressed at all. Even when those specific thoughts are really bothering me, I still get up and go to work every day. I haven't lost interest in anything. I still really care about my job and making sure my clients are taken care of. I try to stay as positive as I can, actually. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, it means I'm handling things okay, right? I just really don't want you to think I'm falling apart or giving up, because I'm not. I'm still doing all the things I'm supposed to do, and keeping up with everything. I'm doing okay with that part, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm staying on track.
